choices.reasoning: All six cards are cheap and useful: Mockingbird (stun+chump), Aunt May (heal), Backflip (defense vs Klaw), Surveillance Team and Interrogation Room (threat removal for the crisis/danger clocks), Spider-Tracer (hoses the Whirlwind minion). Keep the hand.

Round 1 clock check: Main scheme 0/6, threat +1/round now (crisis side scheme blocks thwarting main). Villain Klaw 12 HP (3 stages, 52 total). I'm at 10 HP. Ending in alter-ego gives ~6 threat (instant scheme danger), so I must end in hero. Plan: build Mockingbird (ally + stun Klaw to neutralize his double-boost attack) then clear the crisis side scheme. Play Mockingbird first, stun Klaw.

Pay using Aunt May (dead weight in hero form) + Spider-Tracer, plus Peter Parker's Scientist mental resource (saving a card). Keep Surveillance Team, Backflip, and Interrogation Room — a reusable threat-control package plus defense. Spider-Tracer is the least essential since Interrogation Room covers minion-defeat threat removal reusably.
Stun Klaw so his double-boost attack is fully neutralized this villain phase.
Klaw draws two boost cards on attack, so stunning him prevents the larger, higher-variance hit.

No alter-ego-only actions remain (Aunt May used as fuel), and I must not end in alter-ego (alter-ego threat ~6 = scheme threshold). Change to Spider-Man to use basic powers and act with Mockingbird in hero form. Keep the existing supports/Backflip in hand to redraw into them.

Whirlwind (ATK 2) is the recurring damage source each villain phase — a dangerous minion to remove first per priority. Dealing 2 damage brings him to 4 HP; I'll follow with Mockingbird's attack to get him low.
Keep pressing Whirlwind: Mockingbird's 1 damage brings him to 3 HP, so next turn Spider-Man + Mockingbird can finish him. Trade 1 consequential for faster removal of his recurring 2 damage.

Hero and Mockingbird are exhausted (both power used). Playing Surveillance Team would cost me Backflip (a keep-worthy response card) and Interrogation Room, and at 2 resource cards it's not worth trading a defensive interrupt for. Hold the flexible hand and refill next turn.
